title: [BUG] evp_extra_test fails on NonStop builds in openssl-3.0
body: The openssl-3.0 branch started failing tests on NonStop at or near commit 48fe8d4e53d5572ff77215e3336a1c71b0b4517b. The failure occurs in test/evp_extra_test. I have included the test results and configuration and need assistance diagnosing it.

symptoms_visible: On NonStop, the openssl-3.0 test run fails in test/evp_extra_test; the failure began at or near commit 48fe8d4e53d5572ff77215e3336a1c71b0b4517b.
N0.label: N0 NonStop evp_extra_test failure reported

symptoms_visible: The same test failure occurs in all of my NonStop builds, including the unthreaded 64-bit build.
The expected engine modules exist in the build tree, and the test recipe reports the build-tree engines directory.
N1.label: N1 build mode and module layout established

symptoms_visible: The runtime loads dasync.so and legacy.so from my build tree, not from /usr/local.
Running evp_extra_test -context directly completes its listed tests and then receives SIGSEGV in __process_atexit_functions, exiting with status 139.
N2.label: N2 exit-time SIGSEGV isolated

symptoms_visible: The test still finishes its cases and then receives the same SIGSEGV in __process_atexit_functions when built with OPENSSL_NO_TRACE.
Removing the duplicate trace_data_stack declaration also leaves the exit-time SIGSEGV unchanged.
N2_x.label: N2_x trace cleanup hypotheses falsified

symptoms_visible: My trace prints two registrations of OPENSSL_cleanup during the failing -context process, with the second appearing during test_keylen_change.
All 58 tests report completion, but OPENSSL_cleanup is not printed before the process receives SIGSEGV at exit.
N3.label: N3 duplicate cleanup registration observed

symptoms_visible: The failing process still completes the test cases and crashes only while the NonStop runtime processes exit callbacks after a loaded library has been unloaded.
N4.label: N4 NonStop mixed-linkage exit failure explained

symptoms_visible: A maintainer reports that the change was merged and closes the issue; I have not posted a successful NonStop retest of the merged change.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix merged without reporter verification

question_patterns: Is the failure limited to the SPT build or does it occur in other NonStop configurations?
Which NonStop build modes reproduce this test failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It happens in all of my builds. We normally monitor with the unthreaded 64-bit build, and it happens there too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens in the SPT build; the unthreaded and conventional builds pass.
It reproduces in every build I have tried, but I usually monitor the threaded 64-bit configuration.

question_patterns: Does your usual unthreaded 64-bit monitoring build reproduce it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, the unthreaded 64-bit monitoring build is affected.

question_patterns: Is dasync.so listed in the top-level Makefile's MODULES variable, and which dynamic engines were actually built?
Can you list the engine and provider shared objects present in the build tree?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The top-level Makefile lists engines/dasync.so in MODULES. The build contains capi.so, dasync.so, loader_attic.so, ossltest.so, padlock.so, the shared libraries, the FIPS and legacy providers, and test/p_test.so.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: dasync.so is absent from MODULES and was not produced anywhere in the build tree.

question_patterns: What engine directory does the test recipe report at runtime?
Can you print the engine-related environment value from the recipe?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The recipe prints OPENSSL_ENGINE=/home/<user>/.jenkins/workspace/OpenSSL-3.0_Monitor/engines, which is the correct build-tree directory.

edges.comment: Issue comments c0-c8, all describing the reporter's NonStop systems: the reporter rules out an SPT-only failure, confirms the modules were built, and prints the build-tree engine path.

question_patterns: Can you instrument the runtime library loads and paste the paths passed to dlopen?
Do the actual runtime loads use the configured build-tree paths?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With a printf at dlopen I get ../../providers/fips.so, /home/<user>/.jenkins/workspace/OpenSSL-3.0_Monitor/engines/dasync.so, and /home/<user>/.jenkins/workspace/OpenSSL-3.0_Monitor/providers/legacy.so.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The runtime consistently tries /usr/local/lib64/engines-3/dasync.so and never attempts the build-tree copy.
The same build-tree paths are used, but fips.so is printed as an absolute path too.

question_patterns: Can you run evp_extra_test -context directly with the build-tree library and configuration environment and report its raw exit behavior?
Please run the failing middle command without the Perl test harness and paste what happens.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The direct -context run reaches the last listed tests and then receives signal 11. The wrapper reports '../../util/wrap.pl ../../test/evp_extra_test -context => 139'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The direct command exits 0; status 139 appears only when the Perl harness post-processes it.

question_patterns: Can you capture a debugger backtrace when the direct command receives the signal?
Where is the process stopped when the exit-time signal occurs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The debugger says 'received non-deferrable signal SIGSEGV (number: 11)'. The backtrace starts in __process_atexit_functions, then CRE_TERMINATOR_, exit, and _MAIN.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The backtrace stops inside an EVP cipher operation before the test reports its final cases.

question_patterns: Does the crash occur during a test case or only after the listed cases finish?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The run prints ok 57 and ok 58 before the SIGSEGV. The hang I previously saw was in the debugger, not in the test code.

edges.comment: Issue comments c9-c18, from the reporter's own NonStop run: runtime path tracing retracts the DLL-path red herring, and the handler-requested standalone execution exposes raw status 139 and the exit-time backtrace.

question_patterns: Can you rebuild with OPENSSL_NO_TRACE defined and report whether the exit behavior changes?
As a sanity check, does the failure remain in a build where tracing is disabled?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Building with OPENSSL_NO_TRACE did not change the outcome at all. I get the same SIGSEGV in the same place.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With OPENSSL_NO_TRACE the test exits normally and the SIGSEGV disappears.

solution.intent: Treat the duplicate trace_data_stack declaration in testutil_init as the source of the exit corruption and remove it.
solution.concrete_example: Remove the duplicate declaration of trace_data_stack from testutil_init, rebuild evp_extra_test, and rerun the failing command.

edges.comment: Issue comments c21-c24, reporter's system: disabling trace registration is a handler-requested measurement, while removing the duplicate declaration is an actual local source change. Both leave the same exit-time SIGSEGV, falsifying this trace-specific direction.

question_patterns: Can you add prints around callback registration and execution, then paste the sequence from the failing process?
Please instrument the relevant initialization and cleanup methods and report each registration and invocation.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The failing middle process prints 'Enter ossl_init_register_atexit(OPENSSL_cleanup)' and its exit message once near startup, then prints that registration pair again later in the same process.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing process registers OPENSSL_cleanup exactly once and prints both entry and exit from OPENSSL_cleanup before crashing elsewhere.
The same process prints two registrations, but the second one occurs in a neighboring EVP test rather than test_keylen_change.

question_patterns: At what point in the test output does the second registration appear?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The second OPENSSL_cleanup registration appears inside the test_keylen_change subtest, just before its first iteration is reported.

question_patterns: Do your cleanup entry and exit prints appear before the failing process receives SIGSEGV?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. In the failing -context process all 58 tests finish, then it receives SIGSEGV. My 'Enter into OPENSSL_cleanup' message never appears for that process.

edges.comment: Issue comments c27-c29, reporter's instrumented NonStop build: the raw prints establish two registrations in one process and a crash before the registered cleanup function can visibly execute.

question_patterns: How can the same initialization path register the callback twice in this test process?
Can you explain which separately loaded copies of the initialization state are present?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: As I understand RUN_ONCE, it uses a static variable. That variable has one address in the statically linked module and another in the DLL instance, so each copy can run its initialization.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is only one libcrypto image and one RUN_ONCE state in the process; no static and shared copies are mixed.

question_patterns: What does the NonStop runtime do with registered exit callbacks when a loaded library is unloaded?
How are callback-list entries handled across library unload and later process exit on this platform?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: NonStop has one atexit list in the CRE. When a DLL unloads, its callback entries are invoked but the list is not modified or cleared.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The runtime removes every callback belonging to a DLL as soon as that DLL unloads.

question_patterns: What happens to those retained callback addresses when the main program subsequently exits?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: At main-program exit, the runtime traverses the same list again. The DLL procedure address is no longer accessible, so trying to call it produces SIGSEGV.

question_patterns: Which load during this test introduces the second library image?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The application has the static libcrypto instance, and loading the legacy provider brings in the shared libcrypto instance. That is the static-plus-DLL combination where we have seen this before.

edges.comment: Issue comments c41-c50: participant2 connects the case to the earlier test-suite failure, while the reporter supplies the NonStop-specific RUN_ONCE and CRE callback-list explanation. All affected-system facts in the answers remain the reporter's own account.

solution.intent: Avoid loading a second dynamically linked libcrypto instance in evp_extra_test by statically linking the legacy provider into that test, matching the established treatment for tests that combine static and dynamic linkage on NonStop.
solution.concrete_example: Change the evp_extra_test build so its legacy provider is linked statically, preventing the provider load from introducing a second libcrypto initialization state and a stale DLL exit callback. After the change is merged, rerun the full NonStop openssl-3.0 build and test suite and report whether evp_extra_test exits normally.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted engineering action follows from combining the reporter's runtime evidence with the test's linkage layout: making the legacy provider static prevents a dynamically loaded provider from bringing in a separate libcrypto initialization state. The thread reports that this build change was merged, but it contains no affected-user confirmation after the merge.

edges.comment: Issue comments c52-c56: participant1 proposes statically linking the legacy provider into evp_extra_test; a later replacement change is reported merged and participant2 closes the issue. The reporter began testing an earlier proposal but never posted a successful result, so the terminal state records merge without user verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: evp_extra_test combines a statically linked libcrypto with a shared libcrypto loaded through the legacy provider, giving separate RUN_ONCE state and duplicate exit-handler registration.

Must explain the NonStop-specific failure: the CRE retains a DLL callback entry after unload and attempts to invoke its now-inaccessible address again at main-process exit, causing SIGSEGV in __process_atexit_functions.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the direct exit status and backtrace plus the instrumentation showing two OPENSSL_cleanup registrations; it must not remain focused on an incorrect engine path or a missing dasync.so.
Must not present disabling tracing or removing the duplicate trace_data_stack declaration as the fix, because both were tried without changing the SIGSEGV.
The corrective build change must statically link the legacy provider into evp_extra_test so the test avoids the mixed static/shared libcrypto initialization path.

Must ask the reporter to rerun the NonStop build and tests with the merged change and must not claim reporter-verified resolution, because the thread ends after a maintainer reports the merge without a posted successful retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly experienced NonStop platform maintainer and OpenSSL builder; comfortable rebuilding branches, editing and instrumenting C code, inspecting Makefiles, using gdb/xInspect, tracing dlopen calls, and explaining platform runtime semantics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, direct, and iterative; posts raw logs and backtraces, corrects earlier hypotheses openly, challenges suggestions with platform-specific evidence, and relates current behavior to prior OpenSSL failures.
